name: fairy ring

attributes.attribute: circle of darker green on a grassy field
mark of where fairies danced around their queen

saved a dancer by grabbing clothing outside the ring

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy ring is a folkloric motif. A circle of darker green on a grassy field was held to mark where fairies danced in a ring about their queen. The ring held its charm even when no fairy was present. Livestock were kept off it, and the plow did not touch it. Tales tell of plagues that struck cattle which grazed a fairy ring. Others tell of people who stepped into a ring and danced until they could not stop, some to death. A helper outside the circle could save one only by grabbing a scrap of clothing that reached outside, for anyone who reached in felt the same need to dance.

okr.objective: Fairy ring is a folkloric motif of an enchanted dance circle.
key_results: It marks where fairies danced about their queen.
